question:
A 45-year-old female patient reports a 4-day history of left-sided neck pain. She attributes the
discomfort to sleeping in an awkward position with inadequate neck support from her pillow. She rates
the pain as 5 out of 10 and denies any trauma, radicular symptoms, or numbness. On examination, an
anterior tender point is identified on the lateral aspect of the transverse process of C4 on the left side.
What is the most appropriate counterstrain treatment position for this tender point? Answer Choices:
(A) flexion with sidebending to the right and rotation to the left (B) flexion with sidebending to the left
and neutral rotation (C) flexion with neutral rotation and sidebending (D) extension with neutral rotation
and sidebending (E) extension with sidebending to the left and rotation to the left (F) extension with
sidebending to the right and rotation to the right (G) flexion with sidebending to the right and rotation to
the right (H) flexion with sidebending to the left and rotation to the left (I) flexion with sidebending to the
left and rotation to the right (J) extension with sidebending to the right and rotation to the left
 A. flexion with sidebending to the left and rotation to the right
B. flexion with neutral rotation and sidebending
C. flexion with sidebending to the left and neutral rotation
D. extension with neutral rotation and sidebending
E. flexion with sidebending to the right and rotation to the right
F. extension with sidebending to the right and rotation to the right
G. flexion with sidebending to the right and rotation to the left
H. flexion with sidebending to the left and rotation to the left
I. extension with sidebending to the right and rotation to the left
J. extension with sidebending to the left and rotation to the left
